what_its_for: Brompheniramine is an antihistamine used to relieve symptoms of allergies, hay fever, and the common cold. It helps with runny nose, sneezing, itchy or watery eyes, and itchy throat or skin. It works by blocking histamine, a natural substance your body makes during an allergic reaction.
how_to_take: Take brompheniramine exactly as directed on the label or as your doctor tells you. You can take it with or without food. If it upsets your stomach, try taking it with a small snack or glass of milk. Swallow extended-release tablets or capsules whole — do not crush, chew, or break them. If you are using a liquid form, measure your dose carefully with the measuring cup or spoon provided. Do not use a regular household spoon, as it may give you the wrong amount.
dosing: For adults and children 12 years and older: The usual dose is 4 mg every 4 to 6 hours, or 8 to 12 mg of the extended-release form every 8 to 12 hours. Do not take more than 24 mg in 24 hours. For children 6 to under 12 years: The usual dose is 2 mg every 4 to 6 hours, not more than 12 mg in 24 hours. For children under 6 years: Do not use unless your doctor tells you to. Always follow your doctor's or pharmacist's specific instructions, as doses may vary by product and age.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not double up or take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store brompheniramine at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medications out of the reach of children and pets. Do not use the medication after the expiration date printed on the package. Dispose of unused or expired medicine safely — ask your pharmacist about medication take-back programs.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking brompheniramine, as it can increase drowsiness and dizziness. Do not drive, operate heavy machinery, or do anything that requires you to be fully alert until you know how this medicine affects you. Avoid taking other medications that cause drowsiness, such as sleep aids, muscle relaxers, other antihistamines, or anxiety medications, unless your doctor approves. Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before taking any other cold, allergy, or sleep medicines, as many contain antihistamines and you could accidentally take too much.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency help if you experience: difficulty breathing or swallowing, severe dizziness or fainting, fast or irregular heartbeat, unusual agitation, confusion, or hallucinations (especially in children or older adults), difficulty urinating or no urine output, severe skin rash or allergic reaction. Also call your doctor if your symptoms do not improve within 7 days, if you develop a fever, or if your symptoms come back after getting better.
when_it_works: Brompheniramine usually starts working within 15 to 30 minutes after you take it. The effects typically last 4 to 6 hours for regular tablets or liquid, and up to 8 to 12 hours for extended-release forms. You should notice relief from sneezing, runny nose, and itchy eyes fairly quickly after your first dose.
special_populations: Older adults (65 and older): Use with extra caution. Older adults are more sensitive to the drowsiness, dizziness, and confusion that brompheniramine can cause. It may increase the risk of falls. Ask your doctor if this is the right choice for you. Pregnancy: Talk to your doctor before using this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Breastfeeding: Brompheniramine may pass into breast milk and could harm a nursing baby. Avoid using it if you are breastfeeding, or talk to your doctor first. Children under 6 years: Do not give to children under 6 years unless specifically directed by a doctor. Kidney or liver problems: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver disease, as you may need a lower dose or special monitoring.
